title: Biographical data; family origins; parents' occupations
description: Joy Williams begins the interview by collecting basic biographical information from Alpha Procunier, including her name origin, birth date, and birthplace in Moscow, Idaho. Alpha then provides details about her parents, Ressa Roberts and Daniel Mark, discussing her mother's education at the University of Idaho, her teaching career, and her father's work as a farmer and former traveling photographer. She also mentions her brothers and their current locations.

title: Marriage to Melvin Procunier; children Roberta and Gerald
description: Alpha discusses her 52-year marriage to Melvin Procunier, whom she married at age 20 at her parents' home. She provides details about her husband's background, including his birth in Melrose, Idaho, and childhood in Canada. Alpha then describes their two children, Roberta and Gerald, including their birth dates, births at Mrs. Savage's nursing home in Moscow, and current occupations and residences in Spokane.

title: Education; hobbies and skills; clubs and organizations
description: Alpha outlines her educational background, having completed high school in Moscow. She describes her extensive needlework skills, including quilting, crocheting, and sewing, as well as her outdoor pursuits of raising chickens and gardening. She also lists her numerous community affiliations, including the Grange, Christian Ladies Aid, Bethel Club, Rebecca's, and Senior Citizens, and mentions her husband's participation in the county fiddlers.

title: Marriage duration; rural schooling; Depression-era hardships
description: The conversation turns to Alpha's long marriage and her views on early marriage in rural areas. She describes the challenges of attending high school in Moscow, including living with her aunt and traveling by horse-drawn vehicle. Alpha then discusses how the Great Depression affected her young family, explaining how they survived by raising their own food, keeping cows and chickens, and purchasing secondhand furniture, contrasting their frugality with modern consumer habits.

title: World War II; son's military service; attitudes toward work
description: Alpha reflects on which historical events most affected her life, identifying World War II as particularly significant because she had to send her son Gerald away to military service immediately after his 1945 high school graduation. She discusses the emotional difficulty of this separation. The conversation then shifts to Alpha's philosophy that young people need work to keep them out of trouble.

title: Leisure activities; television; parenting comparisons; childhood memories
description: Alpha describes how she spends her leisure time on embroidery and other handwork, and mentions watching television shows including soap operas, Little House on the Prairie, and The Waltons. She briefly compares her child-rearing experiences with her own upbringing, noting her children had more advantages. She then shares childhood memories of activities with her brothers, including riding a Shetland pony.

title: Educational values; courtship and meeting husband
description: The discussion moves to Alpha's parents' attitudes toward education and her mother's influence as a former teacher. Alpha then recounts the story of how she met her husband Melvin at a barn dance in 1919 when he came to buy a cow from her grandfather, describing their courtship, engagement, and the community social life that brought them together.

title: Childbirth experiences; medical care in the 1920s
description: Alpha describes her experiences giving birth to both children at Mrs. Savage's maternity home in Moscow during the 1920s. She discusses the doctors involved, the use of chloroform and other pain relief methods, her rapid labors, and the lengthy two-week recovery periods that were standard at the time.

title: Family size; children's education and careers
description: Alpha Procunier explains her decision to have only two children due to the cost of education. She describes her daughter's work after high school and her son's military service and business education through the G.I. Bill. She also mentions her five grandchildren and their occupations in healthcare and machining.

title: Birth control; child rearing; infant feeding
description: Alpha discusses learning about birth control from her mother and the limited options available in her era. She describes learning child rearing through experience and her inability to breastfeed, which led to using cow's milk and doctor-prescribed formulas.

title: Changing child behavior; family recreation; winter travel
description: The conversation shifts to how children's activities and behavior expectations have changed over time. Alpha describes family card games and trips to town by horse and buggy, explaining how winter snow blocked roads until the CCC cleared them.

title: Homemaking; farm labor; widowhood concerns
description: Alpha recounts her Depression-era sewing, quilt making, and extensive farm work driving horses and tractors. She reflects on her unpreparedness for potential widowhood given her limited education, and advises young women to maintain their own homes and engage in community affairs.

title: Reading habits; marriage relations; travel
description: Alpha mentions her magazine subscriptions and failing eyesight that limits reading. She describes camping trips to Elk River with her husband, their 52-year marriage, and his lack of interest in her needlework projects.

title: Women's movement; husband's career disappointment
description: Alpha shares her views on women's liberation, supporting equal pay but preferring traditional domestic roles. She reveals her husband's unfulfilled dream of becoming a railroad engineer due to lack of educational funds.

title: Pioneer grandparents; homestead history
description: Alpha recounts her grandparents' 1882 covered wagon journey from Kansas, their initial desire to return upon seeing the hilly terrain, and their eventual settlement on the homestead across the road. She describes their work on the railroad and the establishment of the family land.

title: Early married homes; first car; rattlesnakes
description: Alpha describes moving between various houses early in her marriage and getting stuck in mud with their first Ford car. She also details killing several rattlesnakes around the property, including one she discovered while shaking bedding off the porch.

title: Interview conclusion
description: The conversation winds down as Joy Williams thanks Alpha for the interview and prepares to stop the recording.
